name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
what: Free-floating fuel droplets (heptane, methanol and others) burned on the ISS to map when liquid-fuel flames go out and how well CO₂ and helium suppress them.
key_result: 274 droplet tests; 17 ran at 29-34 % O₂ and about 0.7 atm, the closest any investigation came to the habitat air; CO₂ and helium were tested only up to 25% O₂.
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR
sample: droplet; initial droplet diameter 1.1 mm to 4.7 mm
measurements: LOI, droplet burning rate, extinction diameter, cool flames. Instruments: droplet imaging for burning rate and extinction size, heat radiation, soot and temperature (investigation page goals)
varied: fuel or material: methanol, n-heptane
O₂: 12% to 34% (15 values)
pressure: 0.69 atm to 3.05 atm (182 values)
droplet size: 1.1 mm to 4.7 mm (163 values)
CO₂ added: 0% to 70% (14 values)
helium added: 0% to 45% (10 values)

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiments IV-VI (NASA NTRS 20240002981; not in PSI)
what: Saffire IV to VI on Cygnus: fabric, cotton, acrylic and Nomex burned in reduced-pressure, oxygen-rich air (54-71 kPa, 26-31 % O₂), with cabin CO₂ and CO measured. Published in NASA reports, not in PSI.
key_result: The only solid-fuel burns near habitat air: fabric, cotton and acrylic burned at 26-31 % O₂ and 0.53-0.70 atm, Nomex did not ignite; burning acrylic raised cabin CO₂ by 8,117-8,539 ppm.
hardware: Saffire flight hardware inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
sample: fabric sheet, thick slab (1-sided burning), thick slab (2-sided burning); thickness 0.37 mm to 10.00 mm; width 41 cm; length 7 cm to 50 cm
measurements: far-field CO₂ and CO measurements used for the cabin-air results (Urban et al. 2024, Table 2)
varied: fuel or material: Cotton jersey, Cotton-fiberglass, Nomex fabric, PMMA
sample or burner shape: fabric sheet, thick slab (1-sided burning), thick slab (2-sided burning)
O₂: 22% to 31% (5 values)
pressure: 0.53 atm to 0.99 atm (5 values)
thickness: 0.37 mm to 10.00 mm (3 values)

name: Burning Rate Emulator
what: A porous gas burner that imitates burning solids, run in still air at the spacecraft atmospheres NASA has considered (14.7 psia/21 %, 10.2 psia/26.5 %, 8.2 psia/34 %).
fuels: CH4, C2H4 (pure / 50% in N2) emulating condensed fuels
key_result: Emulated solids kept burning in still air at raised oxygen, while flames at 21 % O₂ went out on their own (investigation page). Daily summaries only, no per-flame results.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: porous burner 25 mm, porous burner 50 mm; size 25.0 mm to 50.0 mm
measurements: heat flux, flame height/radius, radiative fraction, extinction. Instruments: heat-flux sensor and burner surface temperature (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: C2H4, C2H4 50% in N2, CH4
sample or burner shape: porous burner 25 mm, porous burner 50 mm
O₂: 21% to 40% (5 values)
context: Although it burned gas, BRE is a materials-flammability study: the burner imitates a burning solid, in still air, as a function of material properties.

name: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
what: Spherical gas flames (ethane, propane, butane) in a closed, still chamber from 18 to 40 % O₂ and 0.5 to 3 atm: does a flame ignite, and does it go out by itself?
fuels: ethane, propane, n-butane (pure / diluted in N2)
key_result: In still air, all 41 flames at ≤25 % O₂ went out by themselves (median 8 s); at 33-40 % O₂ the median was 50 s and 30 of 91 were still burning when the fuel was cut.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: spherical porous burner (normal flame)
measurements: cool diffusion flame conditions (normal/inverse). Instruments: cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) and thermocouples (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: 30% ethane, 30% n-butane, 30% propane, 50% n-butane (+2 more)
O₂: 18% to 40% (121 values)
pressure: 0.50 atm to 3.00 atm (5 values)
fuel dilution: 0% to 100% (14 values)
fuel flow: 0.00 mg/s to 3.21 mg/s (25 values)
same: sample or burner shape: spherical porous burner (normal flame)
context: CFI-G ran the highest oxygen levels in microgravity: in inverse flames an oxygen-nitrogen mix of up to 85 % O₂ flowed from the burner into a chamber of nitrogen and fuel. Our table holds only the normal flames (fuel from the burner, 18-40 % O₂ around it), which is the cabin-like case.

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
what: Burned fabric (cotton-fiberglass SIBAL), acrylic (PMMA), Nomex, Ultem and candles in a small ISS glovebox flow duct, in air flowing with or against the flame, and tested a CO₂-like extinguishing agent.
key_result: 74 of 110 runs kept burning, 10 went out and 8 never lit; fabric spread up to 5.1 mm/s in the 7.6 cm duct.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE
sample: candle, fabric sheet, sphere, thick slab (+1 more); width 1 cm to 2 cm
measurements: flame spread, extinction, suppression. Instruments: digital still camera through the top window (about 1 frame/s), video camera through the front window (30 frames/s), hot-wire anemometer for flow speed, wide-angle radiometer inside the duct (Ferkul et al. 2013)
varied: fuel or material: Cotton-fiberglass, Japan wax, Nomex III, Nomex blend (+3 more)
sample or burner shape: candle, fabric sheet, sphere, thick slab (+1 more)
O₂: 16% to 23% (39 values)
pressure: 0.97 atm to 1.01 atm (24 values)
air speed: 0 cm/s to 30 cm/s (22 values)
flow direction: concurrent, opposed, stagnation, wake ignition
sample width: 1 cm to 2 cm (2 values)

name: Burning and Suppression of Solids - II
what: Follow-on to BASS: acrylic slabs, rods and spheres, fabric and candles burned at different air speeds and oxygen levels to find when a flame starves or blows off.
fuels: thin/thick flat samples, acrylic slabs, spheres, cylinders
key_result: 129 tests mapped a ‘Goldilocks’ window: 12 flame-outs, from flames starving at low air speed and blowing off at high speed.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE
sample: candle, fabric sheet, rod, slab (+4 more); thickness 0.10 mm to 5.00 mm; diameter 6.3 mm to 40.0 mm; width 1 cm to 2 cm
measurements: flame appearance, growth, spread rate, extinction; O2/CO/CO2 readings. Instruments: video with flow speed, fan and radiometer overlay; Nikon D300s still camera; O₂ sensor; CDM CO₂ sensor and CSA-CP CO analyser (BASS-II data FAQ and science requirements document)
varied: fuel or material: Cotton-fiberglass, Japan wax, Nomex, PMMA
sample or burner shape: candle, fabric sheet, rod, slab (+4 more)
O₂: 14% to 22% (50 values)
air speed: 0 cm/s to 28 cm/s (16 values)
flow direction: concurrent, opposed
thickness: 0.10 mm to 5.00 mm (9 values)
diameter: 6.3 mm to 40.0 mm (4 values)
sample width: 1 cm to 2 cm (2 values)

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II
what: Nine 5 × 29 cm samples (silicone, cotton-fiberglass fabric, acrylic, acrylic joined to Nomex), the same size as NASA's 1 g screening test (NASA-STD-6001 Test 1), burned on Cygnus to compare microgravity flammability limits with that test.
key_result: Silicone burned on Earth but did not spread in microgravity (4 of 4 samples); Nomex did not burn; fabric and acrylic did.
hardware: Saffire flight hardware inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
sample: flat sheet; thickness 0.27 mm to 10.00 mm; width 5 cm; length 5 cm to 29 cm
measurements: low-g flammability limits vs NASA 1 g test. Instruments: two cameras viewing the front of the sample; thermocouples at the duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample and in the plume; radiometers viewing the front and back of the sample; solid-state CO₂, O₂ and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; an anemometer on each side of the sample; a smoke wire at the sample's leading edge for flow uniformity (SAFFIRE-II readme, Table 3: Saffire I, II and III diagnostics)
varied: fuel or material: Cotton-fiberglass, Nomex, PMMA, Silicone
O₂: 21.5% to 22.1% (4 values)
air speed: 20 cm/s to 25 cm/s (2 values)
flow direction: concurrent, opposed
thickness: 0.27 mm to 10.00 mm (6 values)
igniter power: 80 W to 97 W (2 values)
same: sample or burner shape: flat sheet

name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment-I
what: The first large spacecraft fire: a 94 × 40 cm cotton-fiberglass sheet burned inside an empty Cygnus cargo ship after it left the ISS, to see how fast a big fire grows.
key_result: The large fabric sheet burned in microgravity, spreading up to 1.8 mm/s with the flow, at measured cabin pressure.
hardware: Saffire flight hardware inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
sample: flat sheet; thickness 0.37 mm; width 41 cm; length 94 cm
measurements: large-scale flame spread rate, mass consumption, heat release. Instruments: two cameras viewing the front of the sample; thermocouples at the duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample and in the plume; radiometers viewing the front and back of the sample; solid-state CO₂, O₂ and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; an anemometer on each side of the sample; a smoke wire at the sample's leading edge for flow uniformity (SAFFIRE-II readme, Table 3: Saffire I, II and III diagnostics)
varied: O₂: 21.5% to 21.6% (2 values)
flow direction: concurrent, opposed
same: sample or burner shape: flat sheet

name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment-III
what: A second large cotton-fiberglass sheet burned on Cygnus, with flow in both directions.
key_result: The large fabric sheet burned in microgravity, spreading up to 2.3 mm/s with the flow, at measured cabin pressure.
hardware: Saffire flight hardware inside an uncrewed Cygnus cargo vehicle
sample: flat sheet; thickness 0.37 mm; width 41 cm; length 94 cm
measurements: flame spread at different flow conditions. Instruments: two cameras viewing the front of the sample; thermocouples at the duct inlet and outlet, embedded in the sample and in the plume; radiometers viewing the front and back of the sample; solid-state CO₂, O₂ and pressure sensors in the avionics bay; an anemometer on each side of the sample; a smoke wire at the sample's leading edge for flow uniformity (SAFFIRE-II readme, Table 3: Saffire I, II and III diagnostics)
varied: flow direction: concurrent, opposed
same: sample or burner shape: flat sheet

name: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics
what: Droplet cool-flame measurements and simulations (heptane, decane, dodecane) and how outside disturbances change them.
key_result: 72 measurements and simulations of droplet cool flames used in the droplet model.
hardware: model + FLEX data; builds on data from PSI-69; PSI-142
sample: fiber-supported droplet; size 0.5 mm to 7.0 mm
measurements: cool-flame dynamics, extinction diameters, burning rate vs pressure. Instruments: none of its own: a model or analysis investigation that uses data from PSI-69; PSI-142
varied: fuel or material: n-decane, n-dodecane, n-heptane
O₂: 10% to 21% (2 values)
pressure: 0.50 atm to 5.00 atm (8 values)
same: sample or burner shape: fiber-supported droplet

name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
what: Follow-on to FLEX with fuel mixtures closer to real fuels, droplet arrays and soot, over 0.5-3 atm and up to 40 % O₂. PSI lists its condition ranges, not per-test results.
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR
sample: droplet / droplet arrays (catalog, from the NASA page or listing)
measurements: burning rate, sooting, extinction, multi-droplet. Instruments: colour camera video; chamber pressure and temperature (investigation page)

name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight
what: Reflight of SAME with new materials (Pyrell foam), hotter heating and no-flow runs, after SAME's particle samples came back contaminated.
fuels: Kapton, silicone, lampwick (cotton), Teflon, Pyrell foam (heated, not burning)
key_result: 67 smoke test conditions, all in cabin air (21 % O₂, 1 atm); results are in raw files not loaded.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the SAME smoke hardware
sample: heated sample (smoke generator)
measurements: smoke particle sizes vs heating, detector performance. Instruments: the SAME instruments plus a new in-house instrument (M-pass); clean TEM grids after SAME's contamination (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: Kapton, Lampwick, Pyrell, Silicone (+1 more)
air speed: 0 cm/s to 8 cm/s (5 values)
heating time: 60 s to 120 s (2 values)
smoke aging time: 1 s to 720 s (3 values)
same: sample or burner shape: heated sample (smoke generator)
context: One SAME instrument, a modified P-Trak, was used to measure dust in DAFT and DAFT-2.

name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
what: Overheated (not burning) spacecraft materials made smoke in the ISS glovebox, to see how big microgravity smoke particles get and whether smoke detectors notice them.
fuels: Teflon, Kapton, silicone rubber, lampwick, dibutyl phthalate (heated)
key_result: 20 smoke test conditions, all in cabin air (21 % O₂, 1 atm); results are in raw files not loaded.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the SAME smoke hardware
sample: heated sample (smoke generator)
measurements: smoke particle size distribution, detector response. Instruments: two smoke detectors, video cameras, thermophoretic samplers whose particles were sized by TEM after flight (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: Dibutyl Phthalate, Kapton, Lampwick, Silicone Rubber (+1 more)
air speed: 5 cm/s to 10 cm/s (2 values)
same: sample or burner shape: heated sample (smoke generator)
context: One SAME instrument, a modified P-Trak, was used to measure dust in DAFT and DAFT-2.

name: Cool Flames Investigation
what: Droplets of n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures and farnesane, suspended between needles or on silicon-carbide fibres and lit by a retracting hot wire, to study cool flames (the dim low-temperature flame that can outlast the visible one): how pressure, helium dilution and droplet size change burning and extinction, and how soot forms.
key_result: 79 test conditions loaded (conditions only).
hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in the CIR
sample: droplet, droplet (fiber-supported), droplet (free (needle-deployed)); droplets suspended between hypodermic needles or tethered on silicon-carbide fibres; hot-wire igniter retracted after ignition (investigation page)
measurements: cool-flame burning and extinction. Instruments: black-and-white camera for droplet size; UV camera for OH* emission and flame size; narrow-band and wide-band radiometers for flame radiation; high-resolution cameras for monitoring (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: n-dodecane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane 0.60/0.40, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane 0.75/0.25
sample or burner shape: droplet, droplet (fiber-supported), droplet (free (needle-deployed))
O₂: 17% to 21% (2 values)
pressure: 0.50 atm to 5.00 atm (7 values)
helium added: 0% to 59% (3 values)
context: The NASA page lists farnesane and pressures from 0.25 atm; the PSI table we loaded holds n-dodecane and two n-dodecane/iso-dodecane mixtures at 0.5-5 atm (the page itself gives both 0.25-5 and 0.25-0.5 atm). Sponsored by the ISS National Laboratory and NSF.

name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
what: Gas jet flames (methane, ethylene, propane, propylene and propylene mixtures) from 0.41, 0.76 and 1.6 mm nozzles in co-flowing air: the fuel flow was raised until each flame started releasing soot (its smoke point), to measure how burner size, air speed and fuel change sooting.
key_result: 469 fuel-flow settings from 142 flame runs, all in cabin air; smoke points are in raw files not loaded.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE
sample: round jet nozzle 0.41 mm, round jet nozzle 0.76 mm, round jet nozzle 1.60 mm; size 0.4 mm to 1.6 mm
measurements: smoke point, soot formation 0 g vs 1 g. Instruments: still and video cameras; measured flame height (luminous length), radiative heat loss and co-flow air velocity distribution; a flow duct with integrated nozzles and fuel delivery in the glovebox (investigation page)
varied: fuel or material: 50% Propylene, 75% Propylene, Ethylene, Methane (+2 more)
sample or burner shape: round jet nozzle 0.41 mm, round jet nozzle 0.76 mm, round jet nozzle 1.60 mm
air speed: 0 cm/s to 85 cm/s (61 values)
fuel flow: 0.00 mg/s to 4.40 mg/s (275 values)
context: NASA's page gives co-flow speeds of 5.4-65 cm/s and 526 flames; the PSI table we loaded has 469 settings, 26 of them listed outside that speed range (0-85 cm/s). Values are shown as tabulated.

name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling (FGM) vs BASS Two-Color Tomography
what: A computer model of concurrent flame spread compared with BASS flame measurements.
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: model + BASS images; builds on data from PSI-25; PSI-26
sample: flat (catalog, from the NASA page or listing)
measurements: concurrent flame spread model validation. Instruments: none of its own: a model or analysis investigation that uses data from PSI-25; PSI-26

name: Modeling and Simulation of Smoke Generation in Microgravity (SAME data)

hardware: model; builds on data from PSI-102
sample: pyrolysis smoke (catalog, from the NASA page or listing)
measurements: simulated smoke particle growth, 1 g vs 0 g. Instruments: none of its own: a model or analysis investigation that uses data from PSI-102

what: Computational and experimental analysis of the SPICE soot data sets.

measurements: soot temperature/volume fraction (color-ratio pyrometry). Instruments: none of its own: a model or analysis investigation that uses data from PSI-107

name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
what: How gas jet flames anchor and lift off in co-flowing air, for methane, ethylene and nitrogen-diluted mixtures (12 test days).
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG) with the fan-driven flow duct built for SPICE
sample: jet burner tubes in coflow (catalog, from the NASA page or listing)
measurements: flame structure, liftoff, stability. Instruments: over 4,000 high-resolution flame images over 13 test days (investigation page)

name: Flame Design
platform: ISS Combustion Integrated Rack + drop towers
what: Spherical ethylene and methane flames, normal (fuel from the burner) and inverse (oxidizer from the burner), in drop towers and on the ISS: when soot starts to form and when the flame goes out, as flow rate, mixture fraction (Zst), N₂ or CO₂ dilution and pressure change.
fuels: ethylene and methane, with N2 or CO2 inert
geometry: spherical burner, normal and inverse flames; also coflow flames
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: spherical burner for normal and inverse spherical flames; coflow flames as well (investigation page)
measurements: soot-inception and extinction limits, flame temperature, size, colour, soot volume fraction. Instruments: cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes and thermocouples (investigation page)
context: Flame Design also ran inverse spherical flames, where the oxidizer flows from the burner, like the CFI-G inverse flames. Its hypothesis: microgravity spherical flames go out once their peak temperature drops below 1130 K. Tests ran in drop towers as well as on the ISS.

name: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
what: Methane and ethylene flames burning in a gentle coflow of air, from very dilute to heavily sooting, to measure flame shape, lift-off, temperature, extinction limits and soot as velocity and fuel dilution change, and to test computer models of soot.
fuels: methane and ethylene, diluted to sooting
geometry: coflow burner (fuel jet in a coflow of air)
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: coflow burner: a fuel jet surrounded by a slow coflow of air (investigation page)
measurements: flame shape, lift-off height, temperature, extinction limits, soot luminosity, soot temperature and volume fraction. Instruments: OH* and CH* chemiluminescence imaging for lift-off and flame shape; soot luminosity and laser extinction for soot temperature and volume fraction; thin-filament pyrometry for gas temperature (investigation page)
context: E-FIELD Flames (PSI-22) used this same coflow burner for its coflow tests (PSI-22 page).

name: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
what: Methane and ethylene flames (diluted with nitrogen) in an electric field of up to 10 kV between the burner and a mesh above it, with and without a coflow of air: how the field drives ions in the flame, changes its stability and soot, and how fast it responds.
fuels: methane and ethylene, diluted with N2
geometry: gas-jet burner and the CLD coflow burner, with a high-voltage mesh electrode above
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: gas-jet burner, and the coflow burner shared with ACME CLD Flame; copper mesh electrode above the burner (investigation page)
measurements: ion current vs voltage, flame response time, flame shape and luminosity, soot volume fraction, chemiluminescence, radiant emission. Instruments: high-resolution cameras for flame shape, luminosity and soot; spectral imaging with filters for chemiluminescence and soot volume fraction; thermopile detectors for radiant emission; recorded voltage-current curves (investigation page)
context: The challenge brief notes that this experiment mimicked partial gravity: the field acts on the ions that flames make naturally (chemi-ionization) and drives ion-driven convection, a stand-in for buoyancy. Its coflow tests used the same burner as ACME CLD Flame (PSI-21). Per-test data are not in PSI's tables we loaded.

name: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
what: Hydrogen, methane and ethylene, diluted with nitrogen, helium or CO₂, issued from a spherical porous burner into an oxidizing environment: the structure of soot-free and sooty spherical flames, their extinction limits and pulsating instabilities, compared with detailed simulations.
fuels: hydrogen, methane and ethylene, diluted with N2, He or CO2
key_result: Catalogued from its PSI record; per-test results not loaded.
hardware: ACME modular hardware in the Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
sample: spherical porous burner giving a nominally spherical, one-dimensional flame (investigation page)
measurements: flame structure (temperature, species), growth, extinction limits, pulsating instabilities, soot suppression. Instruments: spectrally resolved flame imaging, flame and burner temperatures, radiative flux, and operating conditions (reactant flow rates, ambient temperature, pressure, acceleration levels), all synchronized (investigation page)
